headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed, 24 injured in Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
summary: Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed and 24 others injured in an attack by the Iran-backed Houthi group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The victims include both migrant workers and pilgrims.
details: Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed and 24 others injured in an attack by the Iran-backed Houthi group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The incident occurred as the airport was targeted by Houthi militants.

The two deceased have been identified as Md Shahed Ahmed from Bogura and Md Nasrullah Badarpuri from Cumilla. Shahed, a plumber, was returning to his workplace in Jeddah via Riyadh after a leave, while Nasrullah was on his way to Jeddah for Umrah.

Among the 24 injured, 11 are Bangladeshi migrant workers and 13 were traveling on Umrah visas. They are currently receiving treatment in various hospitals across Riyadh, with the Bangladesh Embassy actively coordinating with hospital authorities to ensure their care.

Three Bangladeshis – Hafez Hasan, Kazi Nurullah, and Md Omar Faruk – are in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Embassy representatives have visited them, and their condition is reported to be stable. Hasan and Nurullah were Umrah pilgrims, while Faruk was a worker.

Other injured individuals include Safat Rahman, who is unconscious, and Md Daudul Islam, both of whom were Umrah pilgrims. Md Saidul Islam Sourav and Abul Mansur Md Riaz Uddin, also Umrah pilgrims, are receiving treatment in another hospital.

Md Abdullah, an Umrah pilgrim from Dhaka, is also among the injured. Additionally, Arman Hossain, Mohammad, and Faisal Ahmed Abdul Haque, with Arman being an Umrah pilgrim and Mohammad and Faisal being migrant workers, are undergoing medical care.

Md Rafiq Mia, a Bangladeshi worker, is also being treated. Three more injured individuals are Ismail Hossain, Md Misbah Uddin Hira, and Md Raihanul Islam, with Ismail and Raihanul being workers. Details for Misbah Uddin Hira are not fully known.

Five other Bangladeshi workers – Salma Akter, Md Shahadat Hossain, Mosahad Ahmed Soikat, Zahid Ahmed, and Sobeh Sadeq Md Shahjahan Sarkar – are also receiving treatment. Md Asadul Islam and Md Jamal, both workers, are also among the injured.

Nazma Akter and two others named Umair and Abdullah Kamil are also reported to be receiving treatment, though confirmed details for Nazma Akter are pending. The Bangladesh Embassy continues to collect detailed information and ensure proper medical attention for all victims.

Following the attack, flight operations were disrupted, leaving approximately 500 Bangladeshi passengers stranded at Riyadh airport. The embassy is working to address the situation and assist those affected by the travel disruptions.

headline_marked: [[NCP announces programs to ensure harmony]] during Durga Puja, protest price hikes
headline: NCP announces programs to ensure harmony during Durga Puja, protest price hikes
summary: The National Citizen Party (NCP) will deploy leaders and activists nationwide to ensure security and communal harmony during the upcoming Durga Puja. They have also announced a week-long public relations campaign and a protest rally against rising commodity pr
details: The National Citizen Party (NCP) has announced a series of programs to ensure security and communal harmony at Durga Puja mandaps across Bangladesh. The party will deploy its leaders and activists nationwide to actively monitor the situation during the upcoming Sharadiya Durga Puja.

These decisions were made during a meeting of NCP's highest policymaking body, the 'Political Council,' held at their party office in Bangla Motor, Dhaka. The meeting was chaired by NCP Convener and Leader of the Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam, with Member Secretary Akhtar Hossain moderating.

A press release from the party's media cell outlined five key decisions. It stated that central and allied organization leaders would remain active in the field to maintain harmony during Durga Puja. Top leaders will also visit puja mandaps in their constituencies and exchange greetings with the Hindu community.

Other decisions include programs protesting the law and order situation, fuel price hikes, rising essential commodity prices, public safety concerns, and corruption in job appointments. These issues are central to the party's public outreach efforts.

NCP will conduct a week-long leaflet distribution and public relations campaign across various locations in Dhaka, starting October 23, to press these demands. This campaign will be inaugurated by Nahid Islam, followed by a protest program on October 30 in Shahbagh, organized by NCP's Dhaka North and South branches.

Regarding organizational matters, the party announced that the restructuring and responsibility allocation of the central committee would be finalized, with a new committee declared by October 13. Additionally, NCP plans to release candidate lists for 100 upazila and municipal local government elections next week, while also intensifying preparations for Union Parishad elections.
